strengths: Technically solid and well-executed: Comprehensive methodology with sophisticated training strategies (curriculum learning, dynamic prior injection, progressive resolution) demonstrated through extensive ablation studies
Extensive experimental validation: Evaluation across 4 major geometric prediction tasks on 15+ datasets with detailed comparisons to recent strong baselines (VGGT, FLARE, AnySplat)
Practical and timely contribution: Addresses real-world need for unified 3D reconstruction framework that flexibly incorporates diverse geometric priors without task-specific specialization

Consistent and substantial improvements: Achieves state-of-the-art or competitive results across diverse benchmarks (10.4-17.8% improvements on point map for 7-Scenes and DTU; significant gains on camera pose, surface normals, and NVS)
Clear presentation and reproducibility: Well-written paper with effective visualizations, comprehensive implementation details in appendices, and promise of code release
Novel framework design: The multi-modal prior prompting mechanism with dynamic injection during training is creative and well-motivated for flexibly handling different prior modalities
Thorough ablation studies: Tables 5-6 convincingly demonstrate the value of different embedding strategies and components for both prior integration and novel view synthesis
weaknesses: Limited fundamental novelty: Core components (DPT heads, transformer decoders, multi-task learning) are standard techniques; novelty primarily lies in their integration and training strategy rather than new methods
Incremental improvements in some areas: While consistent, improvements over VGGT are often modest (2-8 percentage points) in several metrics, suggesting engineering rather than breakthrough advances
Code not yet available: Although promised, current unavailability limits reproducibility verification and broader adoption
Missing computational analysis: No discussion of training time, memory requirements, or inference speed compared to baselines, limiting practical assessment
Insufficient justification for design choices: Dynamic prior injection probability (0.5) and loss function weight selection appear somewhat arbitrary without clear rationale
Limited failure analysis: Minimal discussion of when and why the method fails; Section C acknowledges dynamic scene limitations but lacks detailed error analysis

Generalization claims slightly overstated: Table 7 shows respectable but not superior performance on monocular depth estimation compared to some specialized methods, suggesting universal superiority claims need nuance
Narrow scope of innovation: The key innovation is primarily in prior prompting and integration; the paper is stronger as an engineering contribution than a fundamental methodological advance

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 diverse datasets with multiple output tasks (point maps, camera parameters, depths, normals, 3D Gaussians)
Solid ablation studies examining prior embedding strategies and component necessity, particularly Table 5 comparing dense vs. single-token representations
Visually compelling qualitative results demonstrating effective 3D reconstruction in diverse scenarios (Figures 3, 9-10 with in-the-wild multi-view images)
Well-organized presentation with clear method overview and extensive supplementary material
Addresses a relevant problem: unifying multiple 3D geometric prediction tasks within one model
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core components (token embedding, curriculum learning, dynamic prior injection) are well-established techniques; the paper combines them without fundamental innovation or theoretical justification
Marginal improvements over primary baseline (VGGT, Wang et al., 2025a): most metrics show 1-3% gains, raising questions about practical significance and whether improvements justify added complexity

Overclaimed contributions: 'universal' geometric prediction requires supervised training with all output tasks simultaneously—not fundamentally different from existing multi-task approaches; 'any-prior prompting' reduces to token concatenation

Critical reproducibility gaps: code not available, many unexplained hyperparameter choices (loss weights: λ_cam=5.0, λ_rgb=0.05; prior injection probability at 0.5; exact curriculum learning sequence), complex multi-phase training procedure not fully specified

Lack of theoretical grounding: no explanation for why unified prior prompting should work, why specific loss weights enable universality, or principled justification for design choices—appears largely empirically discovered

Significant practical limitations not adequately addressed: resolution limited to 300-700 pixels, cannot handle scenarios with >1000 input views, suboptimal performance on dynamic scenes and autonomous driving, no reported computational cost or inference speed
Weak ablation on critical design choices: no ablation on loss weight values, curriculum learning ordering, or prior injection probability; Table 6 lacks isolation of individual contribution sources

Inconsistent experimental improvements: performance varies across datasets (tied with VGGT on NRGBD/DTU, marginal gains on novel view synthesis DL3DV at 20.59 vs competitors ~20-21 PSNR), no statistical significance testing or confidence intervals
Missing analysis: no investigation of when/why different priors help, no failure case analysis, no comparison with other multi-task 3D learning frameworks beyond VGGT
Ethical considerations not discussed: privacy implications of 3D scene reconstruction from real images, potential misuse for unauthorized 3D scanning

strengths: Comprehensive multi-task evaluation across 4 geometric tasks and 6+ benchmarks with consistent state-of-the-art or competitive results (e.g., DTU point map: 0.019m vs 0.029m prior best; ScanNet normals: 6.0 vs 10.9+ error)

Novel multi-modal prior prompting mechanism with dynamic injection scheme enabling flexible incorporation of diverse geometric priors (intrinsics, poses, depth) during training, allowing the model to adapt to arbitrary prior combinations

Well-designed curriculum learning strategy addressing multi-task training challenges through systematic task sequencing, data scheduling, and progressive resolution—demonstrating sophisticated engineering
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 5-6) clearly validate design choices and demonstrate contribution of each component
Strong qualitative results showing geometrically consistent reconstructions and improved visual fidelity compared to recent baselines (FLARE, AnySplat)
Reproducibility supported by detailed training procedures, hyperparameters, explicit loss formulations with coefficients, dataset specifications, and promised code/model release
Honest discussion of limitations (resolution constraints, dynamic scene challenges, view scalability, GPU memory constraints) with appropriate acknowledgment of boundaries
weaknesses: Framing as 'unified' framework is overstated—implementation contains substantial task-specific design choices (hybrid normal supervision, specialized 3DGS clustering, different loss formulations) that limit true universality

Novelty is primarily incremental over VGGT; core innovation is integrating prior prompting into existing framework rather than fundamental algorithmic advances building on DPT and conventional multi-task learning

Improvements over baselines, while consistent, are sometimes modest—camera pose estimation shows 99.09 vs 99.97 (not superior), and some monocular/video depth results are only competitive rather than state-of-the-art
Limited analysis of failure modes and sensitivity—no systematic study of performance degradation with missing/low-quality priors, or when dynamic prior injection fails versus specialized methods

Significant practical limitations inadequately addressed: 300-700 pixel resolution constraint is restrictive for real-world applications, cannot handle thousands of input views, unclear computational costs relative to baselines
Some design choices appear arbitrary and lack ablation: 0.5 probability for dynamic prior toggling, loss function weight balancing lacks justification, curriculum task ordering not fully motivated
Required training on 15 diverse datasets for generalization raises questions about model complexity, computational burden, and whether simpler task-specific approaches might be preferable in practice

strengths: Comprehensive unified framework that flexibly integrates diverse geometric priors (poses, intrinsics, depth) while simultaneously predicting multiple 3D representations, addressing a genuine gap between specialized methods
Extensive empirical evaluation across 7 major benchmarks with consistent SOTA or near-SOTA results (10-20% improvements: e.g., Table 1 shows 10.4-17.8% accuracy gains on 7-Scenes/DTU)
Thorough ablation studies validating design choices (prior embedding strategies, curriculum learning, robustness to noise, prior injection methods) with honest performance degradation analysis
Excellent reproducibility: detailed training procedures, hyperparameters, loss functions, hardware requirements, wall-clock training time (70 hours on 32 H20s), and promise to release code
Well-motivated modality-specific tokenization with sensible design (concatenation for global properties, addition for dense depth signals) justified by efficiency and alignment considerations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core components (MLP-based tokenization, curriculum learning, DPT decoders) are standard techniques; primary contribution is their engineering integration rather than novel methods or theoretical insights

Heavy unanalyzed dependence on VGGT pre-training: initialized from pre-trained VGGT weights without ablation isolating new components' contribution from initialization advantage, making actual contribution difficult to assess

Uncontrolled data advantage: trained on 15 diverse datasets while baseline methods use fewer datasets; fair comparison would require identical data, but improvements cannot be cleanly attributed to the method vs. data scale

Fundamental multi-task learning challenges unresolved: recognizes that joint training causes geometry-appearance conflicts but proposes curriculum learning as a workaround rather than addressing root cause; only limited ablation (Table 13)

Limited mechanistic understanding of prior benefits: massive gains with all priors (58.1-53.1% on 7-Scenes/NRGBD in Table 1) lack quantitative analysis of why different modalities help or whether predictions are truly 3D-consistent vs. memorizing priors

Severe robustness issues to realistic noise: Table 12 shows 3.7× accuracy degradation (0.735→2.691) at 0.6× intrinsics noise on DTU; raises concerns for real-world deployment despite claims of robustness
Generalization gaps: 65% worse than π³ on KITTI video depth (0.063 vs 0.038), acknowledged as data bias but unresolved; limited failure case analysis
Novel view synthesis undermines 'unified' claim: explicitly uses ground-truth camera parameters for 3DGS rendering rather than predicted parameters, contradicting feed-forward consistency narrative
Memory scaling problems for practical deployment: 3DGS task scales to only 360 views (60.5GB at 256 views, OOM at 512) while geometry tasks handle 1024 views, severely limiting applicability
Non-negligible inference overhead: full model adds ~13% latency at 64 views (8134.9 vs 7192.2ms) despite efficiency claims; contradicts 'maintaining efficiency' assertion

strengths: Comprehensive evaluation across 5 tasks and multiple datasets with thorough ablation studies and robustness testing
Practical unified system design with reasonable technical choices for multi-modal tokenization and curriculum learning
Extensive reproducibility details including training specifications, loss weights, hardware requirements, and code promise
Extensive supplementary material and additional experiments demonstrating diverse capabilities
weaknesses: Critical confound: model trained on 15 datasets while compared against methods trained on fewer datasets; missing key ablation comparing VGGT with equivalent training data
Overclaimed scope: title promises 'universal' reconstruction but method is limited to 300-700px resolution, cannot handle thousands of views, fails on dynamic scenes and autonomous driving
Incremental novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (VGGT backbone, standard prior injection, curriculum learning) without significant technical innovation or new insights
Core claim that unified architecture enables universal prior benefits is not rigorously validated; cross-task improvements not clearly separated from direct prior effects
Ad-hoc curriculum learning schedule (geometry→normals→freeze,train 3DGS) lacks justification; unclear if this is optimal or generalizable
Modest individual task improvements (5-15%), with NVS gains acknowledged to partially derive from broader training data; underperforms on KITTI
Missing critical comparisons: VGGT with curriculum learning + multi-priors, or Pow3R/MapAnything with same training setup would isolate architectural contributions
Practical limitations downplayed: 3DGS head requires 60.5GB for 256 views, 8+ second inference, 70-hour training on 32 H20 GPUs creates high reproducibility barrier

strengths: Comprehensive experimental validation across 5+ diverse 3D tasks with consistent improvements over strong recent baselines (VGGT, π³, AnySplat)
Addresses genuine practical gap by unifying flexible prior conditioning with multi-task prediction, which prior works addressed separately
Well-demonstrated empirical finding that any prior benefits all tasks (Figure 7), suggesting genuine geometric consistency benefits
Thorough ablation studies covering prior embedding strategies, curriculum learning, robustness to noisy inputs, and hyperparameter sensitivity
Excellent reproducibility with detailed training settings, 15 datasets specified, loss weights provided, and training time documented
Practical utility: feed-forward inference in seconds, modular design, generalizes to 100-200 views despite ≤24 view training
Well-organized presentation with clear motivation, effective figures, and comprehensive appendix
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: heavily builds on VGGT backbone, DPT decoders, and 3DGS rendering; multi-modal tokenization is straightforward (MLPs + concatenation/addition)
Data advantage not cleanly separated: training on 15 diverse datasets likely contributes to improvements, but comparison methods' data coverage not equally assessed
3DGS supervision uses ground-truth camera parameters rather than predicted ones, limiting truly end-to-end claims; impact of this design choice not ablated
Requires complex decoupled sequential training (geometry → normals → 3DGS) that significantly underperforms joint training (Table 13), suggesting unresolved optimization challenges
Underperforms on specialized domain (KITTI autonomous driving: 0.063 vs π³'s 0.038 Abs Rel), limiting universality claims despite being attributed to data underrepresentation
Incomplete baseline comparisons: Pow3R extended to multi-view (unequal comparison), limited MapAnything analysis, no direct comparison with concurrent OmniVGGT
Design choices under-motivated: asymmetric prior handling (pose concatenated vs depth added), loss weight selection (λ values fixed without sensitivity analysis)
Inference speed overhead of ~13% at 64 views described as 'negligible' but is material; 3DGS memory limitations (360 vs 1024 views) underemphasized
